note: Intermediate format — not yet a .lin file. WP3 converts this into a BackupPayload for import via importLinDeck. Content is AI-generated and has not been reviewed by a fluent French speaker yet — treat as a first draft. Each entry has 4 examples: two plain (indicative), one Konjunktiv II (conditionnel), one passive voice. All nouns are annotated with their grammatical gender (masculine/feminine). Common counterparts, opposites, and gender pairs are cross-referenced.

entries.intro: The most fundamental French verb, meaning 'to be'. Used as a copula and as an auxiliary verb for passive voice and certain active verbs in past tenses.
entries.usage: Highly irregular: être, suis, es, est, sommes, êtes, sont. Past participle is 'été'.

examples.translation: I am tired.
He is a doctor.
If I were rich, I would travel.
The house is sold.

entries.intro: One of the two primary auxiliary verbs in French, meaning 'to have'. Used to form compound past tenses for most verbs.
entries.usage: Highly irregular: avoir, ai, as, a, avons, avez, ont. Past participle is 'eu'. Used in idioms like 'avoir faim' (to be hungry).

examples.translation: I have a dog.
She is hot. (Literally: She has warmth)

examples.sentence: Si j'avais le temps, je viendrais.
examples.translation: If I had the time, I would come.
The authorization has been obtained.

entries.intro: First-person singular subject pronoun ('I'). Cross-referenced with 'moi' (stressed), 'me' (#48, object), and 'mon' (#52, possessive).
entries.usage: Elides to j' before a vowel or mute h (e.g. j'ai, j'habite). Must always be lowercase unless starting a sentence.

examples.translation: I speak French.
I love this book.

examples.sentence: Si je pouvais, je le ferais.
examples.translation: If I could, I would do it.

examples.sentence: Je suis invité à la fête.
examples.translation: I am invited to the party.

entries.intro: A highly versatile preposition indicating possession, origin, cause, material, or partition.
entries.usage: Elides to d' before a vowel. Contracts with definite articles: de + le = du, de + les = des.

examples.translation: Marie's book. (Literally: The book of Marie)
He comes from Paris.

examples.sentence: Si je manquais de courage, je partirais.
examples.translation: If I lacked courage, I would leave.

examples.sentence: Le mur est couvert de fleurs.
examples.translation: The wall is covered with/of flowers.

entries.intro: The first particle of standard French negation, typically paired with 'pas' (#6) or other negative words like 'plus' or 'jamais'.
entries.usage: Placed before the conjugated verb, eliding to n' before a vowel. In informal spoken French, it is often omitted.

examples.translation: I do not speak English.
He doesn't like coffee.

examples.sentence: Si tu ne savais pas, tu n'aurais pas dû venir.
examples.translation: If you didn't know, you shouldn't have come.

examples.sentence: Le match ne sera pas annulé.
examples.translation: The match will not be canceled.

entries.intro: The second particle of standard French negation (paired with 'ne' #5). Can also function as a masculine noun meaning 'step' or 'pace'.
entries.usage: Placed after the conjugated verb in negative structures. As a noun: le pas, les pas.

examples.translation: It is not difficult.

examples.sentence: Il fait un pas en avant.
examples.translation: He takes a step forward. (Noun usage)

examples.sentence: Si ce n'était pas si cher, je l'achèterais.
examples.translation: If it weren't so expensive, I would buy it.

examples.sentence: La cible n'est pas encore touchée.
examples.translation: The target is not yet hit.

entries.intro: Definite article for masculine singular nouns. Can also serve as a direct object pronoun meaning 'him' or 'it'. Cross-referenced with feminine 'la' (#8).
entries.usage: Elides to l' before a vowel. Direct object pronoun is placed before the verb (e.g. je le vois - I see him/it).

examples.translation: The dog is black.

examples.sentence: Je le vois tous les jours.
examples.translation: I see him/it every day. (Pronoun)

examples.sentence: Si tu avais le temps, tu le ferais.
examples.translation: If you had the time, you would do it.

examples.sentence: Le livre est lu par l'élève.
examples.translation: The book is read by the student.

entries.intro: Definite article for feminine singular nouns. Can also serve as a direct object pronoun meaning 'her' or 'it'. Cross-referenced with masculine 'le' (#7).
entries.usage: Elides to l' before a vowel. Pronoun is placed before the verb.

examples.translation: The car is red.
I know her well. (Pronoun)

examples.sentence: Si tu connaissais la réponse, tu la donnerais.
examples.translation: If you knew the answer, you would give it.

examples.sentence: La pomme est mangée par l'enfant.
examples.translation: The apple is eaten by the child.

entries.intro: Second-person singular subject pronoun. Used strictly in informal situations (family, friends, children). Cross-referenced with formal/plural 'vous' (#10) and possessive 'ton' (#53).
entries.usage: Subject pronoun. Elides colloquially to t' before a vowel (e.g. t'es instead of tu es - informal only).

examples.translation: You are very kind.
You speak French well.

examples.sentence: Si tu venais demain, tu me verrais.
examples.translation: If you came tomorrow, you would see me.

examples.sentence: Tu es invité par tes amis.
examples.translation: You are invited by your friends.

entries.intro: Second-person plural pronoun ('you all') or polite/formal second-person singular pronoun ('you' respectful). Cross-referenced with informal 'tu' (#9) and possessive 'votre' (#56).
entries.usage: Can represent one person respectfully or multiple people. Verb always takes the '-ez' ending.

examples.translation: What is your name? (Formal)
You are all speaking together.

examples.sentence: Si vous vouliez, vous pourriez le faire.
examples.translation: If you wanted, you could do it.

examples.sentence: Vous êtes attendus dans la salle.
examples.translation: You are expected in the hall.

entries.intro: Third-person singular masculine subject pronoun ('he' or 'it'). Cross-referenced with feminine 'elle' (#12). Also used in impersonal verbs ('il pleut' - it rains).
entries.usage: Subject pronoun. Oblique form is 'lui'.

examples.translation: He lives in Paris.
It is raining today. (Impersonal)

examples.sentence: Si il (s'il) avait faim, il mangerait.
examples.translation: If he were hungry, he would eat.
He is respected by all.

entries.intro: Third-person singular feminine subject pronoun ('she' or 'it'). Cross-referenced with masculine 'il' (#11).
entries.usage: Subject pronoun. Plural form is 'elles'.

examples.translation: She works a lot.
She is very smart.

examples.sentence: Si elle le savait, elle nous le dirait.
examples.translation: If she knew it, she would tell us.

examples.sentence: Elle est soignée par le médecin.
examples.translation: She is treated by the doctor.

entries.intro: Indefinite article for masculine singular nouns. Also represents the number 'one'. Cross-referenced with feminine 'une' (#14).
entries.usage: Invariable as number. Contracts or triggers liaison (e.g. un ami - pronounced with 'n' liaison).

examples.translation: I have a brother.
Only one cake remains.

examples.sentence: Si j'avais un million d'euros, je serais heureux.
examples.translation: If I had a million euros, I would be happy.
A new book is published.

entries.intro: Indefinite article for feminine singular nouns. Also the feminine form of the number 'one'. Cross-referenced with masculine 'un' (#13).
entries.usage: Used with feminine nouns.

examples.translation: She has a sister.
One hour has passed.

examples.sentence: Si j'avais une voiture, je conduirais.
examples.translation: If I had a car, I would drive.
An important decision is made.

entries.intro: Coordinating conjunction used to join words or groups of words. Pronounced as a closed 'é'; the 't' is never pronounced, and never triggers liaison.
entries.usage: Invariable conjunction.

examples.sentence: Toi et moi, nous sommes amis.
examples.translation: You and I are friends.
He is tall and strong.

examples.sentence: Si nous avions du temps et du courage, nous réussirions.
examples.translation: If we had time and courage, we would succeed.

examples.sentence: Le pain et le vin sont servis.
examples.translation: Bread and wine are being served.

entries.intro: A highly common preposition indicating destination, location, time, or possession.
entries.usage: Takes an accent grave (à) to distinguish it from the verb 'a' (has). Contracts: à + le = au, à + les = aux.

examples.translation: I am going to the library.
He lives in Paris.

examples.sentence: Si j'étais à ta place, je dirais oui.
examples.translation: If I were in your place, I would say yes.

examples.sentence: Le prix est attribué à l'artiste.
examples.translation: The prize is awarded to the artist.

entries.intro: Can act as a preposition of place/material or as an adverbial pronoun replacing nouns preceded by 'de'.
entries.usage: As pronoun, placed before the verb (e.g. j'en veux - I want some). As preposition, does not contract.

examples.translation: The box is made of wood.
I have three of them. (Pronoun)

examples.sentence: Si j'en avais le pouvoir, je changerais tout.
examples.translation: If I had the power of it, I would change everything.

examples.sentence: Le cours est dispensé en français.
examples.translation: The course is taught in French.

entries.intro: Functions as a relative pronoun (whom/which), subordinating conjunction (that), interrogative pronoun (what), or comparative adverb (than).
entries.usage: Elides to qu' before a vowel. Used as relative pronoun for direct objects.

examples.translation: I think that he is right. (Conjunction)

examples.sentence: Le livre que je lis est bon.
examples.translation: The book that I am reading is good. (Pronoun)

examples.sentence: Si j'étais plus grand que lui, je serais heureux.
examples.translation: If I were taller than him, I would be happy.

examples.sentence: Il est exigé que la tâche soit faite.
examples.translation: It is required that the task be done.

entries.intro: Relative or interrogative pronoun referring to people or things, acting as the subject of the relative clause. Cross-referenced with direct object 'que' (#18).
entries.usage: Never elides (always 'qui', even before vowels).

examples.sentence: L'homme qui parle est mon père.
examples.translation: The man who is speaking is my father.
Who is there? (Interrogative)

examples.sentence: Si c'était toi qui décidais, que ferais-tu?
examples.translation: If it were you who decided, what would you do?

examples.sentence: Le coupable qui est recherché sera trouvé.
examples.translation: The culprit who is sought will be found.

entries.intro: Preposition of place and time. Specifically denotes being inside an enclosed space or occurring within a timeframe.
entries.usage: Contrasts with 'en' (#17) because 'dans' is typically followed by a determiner (e.g. dans la boîte vs. en boîte).

examples.translation: I am inside the house.
He will leave in ten minutes. (Time)

examples.sentence: Si j'étais dans sa situation, je paniquerais.
examples.translation: If I were in his situation, I would panic.

examples.sentence: Les fleurs sont placées dans le vase.
examples.translation: The flowers are placed inside the vase.

entries.intro: Demonstrative adjective (this/that) or demonstrative pronoun (it/this/that). Used as subject in the common phrase 'c'est' (it is).
entries.usage: Demonstrative adjective inflects: ce (masc), cet (before vowel/h), cette (fem), ces (plural).

examples.translation: This book is very interesting. (Adjective)
It/this is a good idea. (Pronoun)

examples.sentence: Si ce n'était pas vrai, je ne le dirais pas.
examples.translation: If it weren't true, I wouldn't say it.

examples.sentence: Ce travail est fait par des experts.
examples.translation: This work is done by experts.

entries.intro: Preposition of place meaning 'on' or 'above', or indicating topic/subject (about). Distinct from adjective 'sûr' (sure).
entries.usage: Invariable preposition. Triggers liaison (pronounced 'sur' with vowel following).

examples.sentence: La clé est sur la table.
examples.translation: The key is on the table.
An article about economy.

examples.sentence: Si je comptais sur toi, je serais déçu.
examples.translation: If I relied on you, I would be disappointed.

examples.sentence: Le dossier est posé sur le bureau.
examples.translation: The file is placed on the desk.

entries.intro: Preposition indicating purpose, destination, recipient, or cause. Followed by infinitive to mean 'in order to'.
entries.usage: Followed by a noun or infinitive verb (e.g. pour manger - in order to eat).

examples.translation: This letter is for you.

examples.sentence: Il travaille pour gagner sa vie.
examples.translation: He works (in order) to earn his living.

examples.sentence: Si j'étais là pour t'aider, ce serait plus facile.
examples.translation: If I were here to help you, it would be easier.

examples.sentence: Le médicament est prescrit pour la toux.
examples.translation: The medicine is prescribed for the cough.

entries.intro: Coordinating conjunction used to introduce an opposition, reservation, or correction.
entries.usage: Invariable. Often placed between clauses.

examples.translation: He is small but brave.

examples.sentence: Je veux venir, mais je ne peux pas.
examples.translation: I want to come, but I can't.

examples.sentence: Si c'était facile mais long, je le ferais quand même.
examples.translation: If it were easy but long, I would do it anyway.

examples.sentence: La maison est ancienne mais bien entretenue.
examples.translation: The house is old but well maintained. (Passive adjective context)

entries.intro: First-person plural pronoun. Serves as subject ('we'), direct/indirect object ('us'), or reflexive pronoun ('ourselves'). Cross-referenced with possessive 'notre' (#55).
entries.usage: Pronounced 'noo' (or 'nooz' before vowels). Oblique/stressed form is also 'nous'.

examples.translation: We are learning French. (Subject)
He looks at us. (Object)

examples.sentence: Si nous le voulions, nous pourrions voyager.
examples.translation: If we wanted, we could travel.
We are welcomed warmly.

entries.intro: Third-person plural masculine subject pronoun. Used for groups of males or mixed groups (even if only one male is present). Cross-referenced with feminine 'elles' (#27) and possessive 'leur' (#51).
entries.usage: Takes plural verb endings (e.g. ils parlent). The final 's' is silent except in liaison ('ilz').

examples.translation: They are going to the cinema.
They are studying physics.
If they knew, they would come.

examples.sentence: Ils sont protégés par la loi.
examples.translation: They are protected by the law.

entries.intro: Third-person plural feminine subject pronoun. Used strictly for groups of all-female people or all-feminine objects. Cross-referenced with masculine 'ils' (#26).
entries.usage: Takes plural verb endings. final 's' is silent except in liaison.

examples.translation: They are sisters.
They are reading books.

examples.sentence: Si elles partaient maintenant, elles arriveraient à l'heure.
examples.translation: If they left now, they would arrive on time.
They are invited to dinner.

entries.intro: Indefinite third-person singular subject pronoun meaning 'one', 'people', or very commonly used in modern spoken French for 'we'.
entries.usage: Takes singular verb agreement (like il/elle), but context determines if it refers to 'we' (plural) or 'one' (singular).

examples.translation: We are going to the beach. (Informal/Spoken)
French is spoken here. / One speaks French here.

examples.sentence: Si on travaillait ensemble, ce serait mieux.
examples.translation: If we worked together, it would be better.

examples.sentence: On est souvent trompé par les apparences.
examples.translation: One is often deceived by appearances.

entries.intro: Highly versatile word meaning 'all', 'every', 'everything', or 'entirely'.
entries.usage: Inflects: tout (masc sing), toute (fem sing), tous (masc plur - final 's' pronounced when pronoun), toutes (fem plur).

examples.translation: Everyone is here. (Literally: All the world)
I understand everything. (Pronoun)

examples.sentence: Si tout allait bien, je ne me plaindrais pas.
examples.translation: If everything went well, I wouldn't complain.
The entire cake is eaten.

entries.intro: Adverb used to express superiority (more) or negation (no more / no longer, paired with 'ne').
entries.usage: Pronunciation of final 's': pronounced ('pluss') in positive comparative contexts, silent ('plu') in negative contexts.

examples.sentence: Il est plus grand que moi.
examples.translation: He is taller (more tall) than me. (Final 's' is silent)
I have no more money. (Negation)

examples.sentence: Si j'avais plus de temps, je lirais plus.
examples.translation: If I had more time, I would read more. (Final 's' is pronounced in 'plus de')
The decision is no longer contested.

entries.intro: Highly common verb meaning 'to do' or 'to make'. Used in numerous idioms and causative constructions.
entries.usage: Irregular verb: faire, fais, fait, faisons, faites, font. Past participle is 'fait'.

examples.translation: I am doing my homework.
She is making a cake.

examples.sentence: Si je savais le faire, je t'aiderais.
examples.translation: If I knew how to do it, I would help you.

examples.sentence: Le travail est fait avec soin.
examples.translation: The work is done with care.

entries.intro: Common verb meaning 'to say' or 'to tell'.
entries.usage: Irregular verb: dire, dis, dit, disons, dites, disent. Past participle is 'dit'.

examples.translation: What are you saying?
He says the truth.

examples.sentence: Si je le savais, je te le dirais.
examples.translation: If I knew it, I would tell you.
The truth is finally told.

entries.intro: Modal verb expressing ability, capability, or permission. Can also be a masculine noun meaning 'power' (#346).
entries.usage: Highly irregular: pouvoir, peux, peut, pouvons, pouvez, peuvent. Past participle is 'pu'. Followed by infinitive.

examples.translation: I can speak Spanish.
Can we come in?

examples.sentence: Si je le pouvais, je viendrais avec plaisir.
examples.translation: If I could, I would come with pleasure.

examples.sentence: Cette tâche peut être accomplie rapidement.
examples.translation: This task can be accomplished quickly.

entries.intro: Modal verb expressing desire, wish, or will.
entries.usage: Highly irregular: vouloir, veux, veut, voulons, voulez, veulent. Past participle is 'voulu'. Polite request uses conditionnel 'voudrais'.

examples.translation: I want to eat now.
He wants to succeed.

examples.sentence: Je voudrais un verre d'eau, s'il vous plaît.
examples.translation: I would like a glass of water, please.

examples.sentence: Ce changement est voulu par tous.
examples.translation: This change is wanted by everyone.

entries.intro: Modal verb indicating obligation, necessity, or probability. Can also be a masculine noun meaning 'duty' or 'homework'.
entries.usage: Irregular verb: devoir, dois, doit, devons, devez, doivent. Past participle is 'dû'.

examples.translation: I have to work tonight.
He does his homework.

examples.sentence: Tu devrais te reposer un peu.
examples.translation: You should rest a bit. (Polite obligation)

examples.sentence: Le rapport doit être soumis avant midi.
examples.translation: The report must be submitted before noon.

entries.intro: Extremely common verb meaning 'to go'. Also acts as auxiliary to form the near future (futur proche).
entries.usage: Irregular -er verb: aller, vais, vas, va, allons, allez, vont. Requires auxiliary 'être' in past compound tenses.

examples.translation: I am going to the supermarket.
She is going to leave soon. (Near future)

examples.sentence: Si j'allais là-bas, je le verrais.
examples.translation: If I went there, I would see him.
The path is traced. (Passive context of going/routing)

entries.intro: Common verb meaning 'to come'. Paired with 'de' to form the recent past (passé récent). Opposite of 'aller' (#36).
entries.usage: Highly irregular: venir, viens, vient, venons, venez, viennent. Past participle is 'venu'. Requires auxiliary 'être'.

examples.translation: I am coming from my place.
He has just eaten. (Recent past)

examples.sentence: Si tu venais ce soir, on dînerait ensemble.
examples.translation: If you came tonight, we would dine together.

examples.sentence: La marchandise est venue de loin.
examples.translation: The merchandise came from far away. (Intransitive, passive context)

entries.intro: Verb of perception meaning 'to see' or 'to understand'.
entries.usage: Irregular verb: voir, vois, voit, voyons, voyez, voient. Past participle is 'vu'.

examples.sentence: Je vois un oiseau dans le ciel.
examples.translation: I see a bird in the sky.

examples.sentence: Ah, je vois ce que tu veux dire.
examples.translation: Ah, I see what you mean.

examples.sentence: Si je le voyais, je l'appellerais.
examples.translation: If I saw him, I would call him.

examples.sentence: Le film est vu par des millions de gens.
examples.translation: The movie is seen by millions of people.

entries.translation: to know (a fact / how to do)
entries.intro: Verb meaning 'to know' information/facts or 'to know how to' perform an action. Cross-referenced with 'connaître' (to know people/places).
entries.usage: Irregular verb: savoir, sais, sait, savons, savez, savent. Past participle is 'su'.

examples.translation: I know how to read.

examples.sentence: Il sait que tu es là.
examples.translation: He knows that you are here.

examples.sentence: Si je savais son numéro, je l'appellerais.
examples.translation: If I knew his number, I would call him.

examples.sentence: Le secret est connu de tous.
examples.translation: The secret is known by all. (Derived from connaître/savoir passive)

entries.intro: Very common verb meaning 'to take', 'to catch', or 'to eat/drink' (meals).
entries.usage: Irregular verb: prendre, prends, prend, prenons, prenez, prennent. Past participle is 'pris'.

examples.sentence: Je prends le bus tous les matins.
examples.translation: I take the bus every morning.
He has his coffee.

examples.sentence: Si tu prenais le temps, tu réussirais.
examples.translation: If you took the time, you would succeed.
The decision is taken.

entries.intro: Standard French verb meaning 'to give'. Cross-referenced with 'prendre' (#40).
entries.usage: Regular -er verb. Past participle is 'donné'.

examples.sentence: Je donne un livre à mon ami.
examples.translation: I give a book to my friend.
She gives useful advice.

examples.sentence: Si tu lui donnais une chance, il s'excuserait.
examples.translation: If you gave him a chance, he would apologize.

examples.sentence: L'autorisation est donnée par le directeur.
examples.translation: The authorization is given by the director.

entries.intro: Preposition indicating accompaniment, association, or instrument.
entries.usage: Invariable. Triggers liaison in formal speech (e.g. avec un ami).

examples.sentence: Je vais au marché avec ma mère.
examples.translation: I go to the market with my mother.

examples.sentence: Il écrit avec un stylo plume.
examples.translation: He writes with a fountain pen.

examples.sentence: Si je voyageais avec toi, je serais heureux.
examples.translation: If I traveled with you, I would be happy.

examples.sentence: Le café est servi avec du sucre.
examples.translation: The coffee is served with sugar.

entries.intro: Preposition indicating absence or exclusion. Opposite of 'avec' (#42).
entries.usage: Invariable. Followed by a noun or an infinitive (e.g. sans manger - without eating).

examples.sentence: Il boit son café sans sucre.
examples.translation: He drinks his coffee without sugar.

examples.sentence: Elle est partie sans dire un mot.
examples.translation: She left without saying a word.

examples.sentence: Si j'étais sans amis, je m'ennuierais.
examples.translation: If I were without friends, I would be bored.
The exercise is done without a calculator.

entries.intro: Indicates comparison (like/as), role (as), or cause (since).
entries.usage: Invariable. When introducing a cause, it must be at the beginning of the sentence.

examples.translation: He runs like a rabbit. (Comparison)

examples.sentence: Comme il pleut, je reste chez moi.
examples.translation: Since it is raining, I am staying home. (Cause)

examples.sentence: Si j'agissais comme toi, je serais blâmé.
examples.translation: If I acted like you, I would be blamed.

examples.sentence: Cette maison est utilisée comme musée.
examples.translation: This house is used as a museum.

entries.intro: Conjunction introducing a condition (if), adverb of intensity (so), or response confirming a negative question (yes).
entries.usage: Elides to s' only before 'il' or 'ils' (s'il, s'ils).

examples.translation: If you study, you will succeed. (Condition)
Yes indeed, I saw him! (Contradicting a negative statement)

examples.sentence: Si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu.
examples.translation: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.

examples.sentence: Le match sera rejoué si la pluie s'arrête.
examples.translation: The match will be replayed if the rain stops.

entries.intro: Adverbial pronoun replacing a place preceded by 'à' or a preposition of location (there), or replacing a noun introduced by 'à'.
entries.usage: Placed before the verb (e.g. j'y vais - I'm going there). Commonly used in 'il y a' (there is/are).

examples.sentence: Il y a un chat dans le jardin.
examples.translation: There is a cat in the garden. (Idiom: il y a)
I think about it/to it often. (Pronoun)

examples.sentence: Si j'y allais, je serais perdu.
examples.translation: If I went there, I would be lost.
The project is integrated into it.

entries.intro: Third-person singular/plural reflexive pronoun. Used with pronominal verbs.
entries.usage: Placed directly before the verb. Elides to s' before a vowel.

examples.translation: He washes his hands.
They look at each other.

examples.sentence: Si elle se couchait tôt, elle serait en forme.
examples.translation: If she went to bed early, she would be in shape.
History repeats itself. (Pronominal passive context)

entries.intro: First-person singular reflexive or object pronoun. Cross-referenced with 'je' (#3) and stressed 'moi'.
entries.usage: Placed before the verb. Elides to m' before a vowel.

examples.sentence: Il me parle de ses projets.
examples.translation: He is talking to me about his plans.

examples.sentence: Je me lève à six heures.
examples.translation: I get myself up at six o'clock.

examples.sentence: Si tu me le demandais, je le ferais.
examples.translation: If you asked me (for it), I would do it.

examples.sentence: Un cadeau m'est donné par mon frère.
examples.translation: A gift is given to me by my brother.

entries.intro: Second-person singular informal reflexive or object pronoun. Cross-referenced with 'tu' (#9) and stressed 'toi'.
entries.usage: Placed before the verb. Elides to t' before a vowel.

examples.sentence: Je te donnerai le livre demain.
examples.translation: I will give you the book tomorrow.
You wash yourself.

examples.sentence: Si je te voyais triste, je t'aiderais.
examples.translation: If I saw you sad, I would help you.
This letter is sent to you.

entries.translation: him / her / to him / to her
entries.intro: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun (to him / to her) or stressed pronoun (him).
entries.usage: Stressed pronoun placed after prepositions (pour lui). Indirect object pronoun placed before verb (je lui parle).

examples.sentence: Je lui parle tous les jours.
examples.translation: I talk to him/her every day. (Indirect object)
This bag is his. (Stressed)

examples.sentence: Si tu lui écrivais, il répondrait.
examples.translation: If you wrote to him, he would reply.
The floor is given to him/her.

entries.intro: Can act as a possessive adjective (their) or as a third-person plural indirect object pronoun (to them).
entries.usage: As pronoun, invariable and placed before the verb (je leur dis). As adjective, takes 's' in plural (leurs).

examples.translation: I give them advice. (Pronoun)
It is their house. (Adjective)

examples.sentence: Si tu leur parlais, ils comprendraient.
examples.translation: If you talked to them, they would understand.
A prize is awarded to them.

entries.intro: Masculine singular possessive adjective. Cross-referenced with feminine 'ma' (#57) and plural 'mes' (#60).
entries.usage: Used before masculine singular nouns, and also before feminine singular nouns starting with a vowel/mute h (e.g. mon amie).

examples.translation: It is my favorite book.
My (female) friend lives in Lyon. (Feminine noun starting with vowel)

examples.sentence: Si mon père était là, il serait fier.
examples.translation: If my father were here, he would be proud.

examples.sentence: Mon sac est gardé à la consigne.
examples.translation: My bag is kept in the cloakroom.

entries.intro: Second-person singular possessive adjective. Can also be a masculine noun meaning 'tone' or 'pitch'. Cross-referenced with feminine 'ta' (#58) and plural 'tes' (#61).
entries.usage: Possessive adjective used before masculine singular nouns or feminine singular nouns starting with a vowel.

examples.translation: Where is your bag?
I like your writing tone.

examples.sentence: Si ton frère venait, ce serait amusant.
examples.translation: If your brother came, it would be fun.

examples.sentence: Ton avis est demandé par l'équipe.
examples.translation: Your opinion is requested by the team.

entries.intro: Third-person singular possessive adjective. Can also be a masculine noun meaning 'sound'. Cross-referenced with feminine 'sa' (#59) and plural 'ses' (#62).
entries.usage: Adjective agrees with the possessed noun, not the owner (e.g. son livre - his/her book). Used before vowels.

examples.translation: It is his/her coat.

examples.sentence: Le son de la musique est fort. (Noun usage)
examples.translation: The sound of the music is loud.

examples.sentence: Si son projet était prêt, il le présenterait.
examples.translation: If his/her project were ready, he/she would present it.

examples.sentence: Son travail est apprécié de tous.
examples.translation: His/Her work is appreciated by all.

entries.intro: Possessive adjective for first-person plural, used with singular nouns. Cross-referenced with plural possessive 'nos' (#63).
entries.usage: Used for both masculine and feminine singular nouns. Plural form is 'nos'.

examples.translation: Here is our house.
Our teacher is absent.

examples.sentence: Si notre équipe gagnait, on fêterait.
examples.translation: If our team won, we would celebrate.
Our project is validated.

entries.intro: Possessive adjective for second-person formal or plural, used with singular nouns. Cross-referenced with plural possessive 'vos' (#64).
entries.usage: Used for both masculine and feminine singular nouns.

examples.translation: Where is your car?
It is your choice.

examples.sentence: Si votre ami venait, nous serions ravis.
examples.translation: If your friend came, we would be delighted.

examples.sentence: Votre passeport est demandé à l'entrée.
examples.translation: Your passport is requested at the entrance.

entries.intro: Feminine singular possessive adjective. Cross-referenced with masculine 'mon' (#52) and plural 'mes' (#60).
entries.usage: Used strictly before feminine singular nouns starting with a consonant (e.g. ma sœur).

examples.translation: It is my car.
My mother lives here.

examples.sentence: Si ma sœur était libre, elle viendrait.
examples.translation: If my sister were free, she would come.
My suitcase is lost.

entries.intro: Second-person singular feminine possessive adjective. Cross-referenced with masculine 'ton' (#53) and plural 'tes' (#61).
entries.usage: Used before feminine singular nouns starting with a consonant.

examples.translation: This is your bedroom.
Your mother is calling you.

examples.sentence: Si ta valise était trop lourde, je la porterais.
examples.translation: If your suitcase were too heavy, I would carry it.
Your candidacy is accepted.

entries.intro: Third-person singular feminine possessive adjective. Cross-referenced with masculine 'son' (#54) and plural 'ses' (#62).
entries.usage: Agrees with the possessed feminine noun (e.g. sa table).

examples.translation: It is his/her guitar.
His/Her house is large.

examples.sentence: Si sa voiture tombait en panne, il prendrait le train.
examples.translation: If his/her car broke down, he/she would take the train.

examples.sentence: Sa voix est entendue par tout le monde.
examples.translation: His/Her voice is heard by everyone.

entries.intro: Possessive adjective for first-person singular plural nouns. Cross-referenced with singular 'mon' (#52) and 'ma' (#57).
entries.usage: Used for both masculine and feminine plural nouns. Triggers 'z' liaison before vowels.

examples.translation: Where are my keys?
My friends live in Paris. (Liaison: 'mezami')

examples.sentence: Si mes notes étaient meilleures, je serais heureux.
examples.translation: If my grades were better, I would be happy.
My luggage is checked in.

entries.intro: Possessive adjective for second-person singular plural nouns. Cross-referenced with singular 'ton' (#53) and 'ta' (#58).
entries.usage: Used for plural nouns owned by 'tu'.

examples.translation: Here are your things.
Your parents are kind.

examples.sentence: Si tes devoirs étaient faits, tu pourrais sortir.
examples.translation: If your homework were done, you could go out.

examples.sentence: Tes idées sont acceptées par le comité.
examples.translation: Your ideas are accepted by the committee.

entries.intro: Possessive adjective for third-person singular plural nouns. Cross-referenced with singular 'son' (#54) and 'sa' (#59).
entries.usage: Agrees with the possessed plural nouns.

examples.translation: He puts away his clothes.
His/Her eyes are blue.

examples.sentence: Si ses amis étaient là, il ferait la fête.
examples.translation: If his/her friends were here, he/she would party.

examples.sentence: Ses droits sont protégés par la constitution.
examples.translation: His/Her rights are protected by the constitution.

entries.intro: Possessive adjective for first-person plural, used with plural nouns. Cross-referenced with singular 'notre' (#55).
entries.usage: Used for all plural nouns owned by 'nous'.

examples.translation: Here is our luggage.
Our friends are arriving tonight.

examples.sentence: Si nos plans changeaient, nous t'avertirions.
examples.translation: If our plans changed, we would warn you.

examples.sentence: Nos projets sont financés par l'État.
examples.translation: Our projects are funded by the State.

entries.intro: Possessive adjective for second-person plural or formal singular, used with plural nouns. Cross-referenced with singular 'votre' (#56).
entries.usage: Used for plural nouns owned by 'vous'.

examples.translation: Where are your children?
I am waiting for your answers.

examples.sentence: Si vos billets étaient perdus, il faudrait en racheter.
examples.translation: If your tickets were lost, you would have to buy new ones.
Your data is backed up.

entries.intro: A masculine noun indicating either duration/period (time) or atmospheric conditions (weather).
entries.usage: le temps, les temps (plural remains the same). 'avoir le temps' (to have time), 'quel temps fait-il?' (how is the weather?).

examples.translation: I do not have time.
What beautiful weather today!

examples.sentence: Si le temps s'arrêtait, je profiterais de l'instant.
examples.translation: If time stopped, I would enjoy the moment.

examples.sentence: Le temps de travail est réglementé.
examples.translation: Working time is regulated.

entries.intro: A general feminine noun for an object, matter, or event. 'quelque chose' means 'something'.
entries.usage: la chose, les choses. Used heavily in everyday phrases.

examples.translation: It is a good thing.
He tells interesting things.

examples.sentence: Une telle chose serait impossible ici.
examples.translation: Such a thing would be impossible here.
Things are clarified.

entries.intro: An adult male human or mankind in general (with capital H). Cross-referenced with feminine 'femme' (#68).
entries.usage: l'homme (requires elision), les hommes. 'droits de l'homme' (human rights).

examples.translation: This man is my uncle.

examples.sentence: L'Homme a marché sur la lune.
examples.translation: Man walked on the moon.

examples.sentence: Si cet homme avait du courage, il parlerait.
examples.translation: If this man had courage, he would speak.
The man is treated at the hospital.

entries.intro: An adult female human or a married female partner. Cross-referenced with masculine 'homme' (#67).
entries.usage: la femme, les femmes. Pronounced 'fam'.

examples.translation: She is a very dynamic woman.
I present my wife to you.
A more patient woman would understand.
The woman is elected president.

entries.intro: A person with whom one has a bond of friendship. Feminine form is 'amie'.
entries.usage: l'ami, les amis. Oblique/possessive is 'mon ami' (even for females, for sound reasons).

examples.translation: He is my best friend.
I am going out with my friends.

examples.sentence: Si j'avais un ami sincère, je lui confierais mon secret.
examples.translation: If I had a sincere friend, I would confide my secret to him.

examples.sentence: L'ami est accueilli à bras ouverts.
examples.translation: The friend is welcomed with open arms.

entries.intro: A 24-hour period or the daylight hours. Cross-referenced with 'nuit' (#71).
entries.usage: le jour, les jours. 'tous les jours' (every day), 'le jour J' (D-day).

examples.translation: It is a great day.
He works during the day.

examples.sentence: Un jour plus ensoleillé serait parfait.
examples.translation: A sunnier day would be perfect.

examples.sentence: Le jour de l'an est célébré partout.
examples.translation: New Year's Day is celebrated everywhere.

entries.intro: The period of darkness from sunset to sunrise. Cross-referenced with 'jour' (#70).
entries.usage: la nuit, les nuits. 'bonne nuit' (good night).

examples.translation: The night is calm.
He reads during the night.

examples.sentence: Si la nuit était plus claire, on verrait les étoiles.
examples.translation: If the night were clearer, we would see the stars.

examples.sentence: La nuit est souvent troublée par l'orage.
examples.translation: The night is often disturbed by the storm.

entries.intro: The liquid substance forming rain, rivers, and seas.
entries.usage: l'eau, les eaux (plural spelling with 'x'). Uncountable singular.

examples.translation: I drink water.
The lake's water is cold.

examples.sentence: De l'eau plus chaude serait agréable.
examples.translation: Warmer water would be pleasant.

examples.sentence: L'eau est polluée par les usines.
examples.translation: The water is polluted by factories.

entries.intro: Describes large physical size, height in people, or moral greatness. Cross-referenced with 'petit' (#74).
entries.usage: Inflects: grand (masc), grande (fem), grands (masc plur), grandes (fem plur). Placed before the noun.

examples.translation: He is a great man.
He has a big house.

examples.sentence: Un plus grand jardin plairait aux enfants.
examples.translation: A bigger garden would please the children.

examples.sentence: Le projet est mené à grande échelle.
examples.translation: The project is conducted on a large scale.

entries.intro: Describes small size, stature, or younger age. Cross-referenced with 'grand' (#73).
entries.usage: Inflects: petit (masc), petite (fem), petits (masc plur), petites (fem plur). Placed before the noun.

examples.translation: He has a small cat.
She is my little sister.

examples.sentence: Un plus petit sac serait plus pratique.
examples.translation: A smaller bag would be more practical.

examples.sentence: Les petits détails sont souvent oubliés.
examples.translation: The small details are often forgotten.

entries.intro: Refers to high quality, pleasant taste, moral goodness, or correctness. Cross-referenced with 'mauvais' (#76) and adverb 'bien' (#77).
entries.usage: Inflects: bon (masc), bonne (fem), bons (masc plur), bonnes (fem plur). Placed before the noun.

examples.translation: This chocolate is very good.
It is a good idea.

examples.sentence: Un bon vin accompagnerait bien le repas.
examples.translation: A good wine would go well with the meal.

examples.sentence: Le bon candidat est enfin choisi.
examples.translation: The right candidate is finally chosen.

entries.intro: Refers to poor quality, unpleasantness, or moral wrongness. Cross-referenced with 'bon' (#75) and adverb 'mal' (#78).
entries.usage: Inflects: mauvais (masc sing/plur), mauvaise (fem sing), mauvaises (fem plur). Placed before the noun.

examples.translation: It is a bad movie.
The weather is bad today. (Idiom)
A bad decision would ruin everything.
Bad behaviors are punished.

entries.intro: The standard adverb meaning 'well'. Can also function as a masculine noun meaning 'property' or 'moral good'. Cross-referenced with 'bon' (#75) and 'mal' (#78).
entries.usage: Invariable adverb. Modify verbs or adjectives ('très bien').

examples.translation: He speaks French very well.
It is for your own good.

examples.sentence: Je me sentirais bien mieux si tu venais.
examples.translation: I would feel much better if you came.
The lesson is well understood.

entries.intro: The standard adverb meaning 'badly'. Can also act as a masculine noun meaning 'pain', 'difficulty', or 'evil'. Cross-referenced with 'bien' (#77).
entries.usage: Invariable adverb. 'avoir mal' (to have pain/hurt), 'faire mal' (to hurt).

examples.translation: He writes badly.
I have a headache. (Literally: pain at the head)

examples.sentence: Tu aurais du mal à le croire.
examples.translation: You would have difficulty believing it.
The project is poorly designed.

entries.intro: Adverb of place indicating proximity to the speaker. Cross-referenced with 'là' (#80) and 'où' (#81).
entries.usage: Invariable. Often paired with 'là' (ici et là - here and there).

examples.translation: Come here.
It is warm here.

examples.sentence: Si j'habitais ici, je serais ravi.
examples.translation: If I lived here, I would be delighted.
French is taught here.

entries.intro: Adverb of place indicating a distant location. In everyday spoken French, it is often used interchangeably with 'ici' (here).
entries.usage: Takes accent grave (là) to distinguish from article 'la' (#8). 'être là' (to be here/present).

examples.translation: I will be there/here tomorrow.
Who is there?

examples.sentence: Si tu allais là, tu verrais la mer.
examples.translation: If you went there, you would see the sea.

examples.sentence: Une nouvelle école est construite là.
examples.translation: A new school is being built there.

entries.intro: Relative pronoun or interrogative adverb of place (where) or time (when / which).
entries.usage: Takes accent grave (où) to distinguish from conjunction 'ou' (or).

examples.translation: Where are you going? (Interrogative)

examples.sentence: Le jour où je suis né.
examples.translation: The day when I was born. (Relative)

examples.sentence: Si je savais où il habite, je le visiterais.
examples.translation: If I knew where he lives, I would visit him.

examples.sentence: L'endroit où le crime a été commis est bouclé.
examples.translation: The place where the crime was committed is cordoned off.

entries.intro: Subordinating conjunction or interrogative adverb of time.
entries.usage: Pronounced with 't' liaison before a vowel (e.g. quand il - pronounced 'kantil').

examples.translation: When will you come? (Interrogative)

examples.sentence: Je dors quand je suis fatigué. (Conjunction)
examples.translation: I sleep when I am tired.

examples.sentence: Si tu venais quand je t'invite, ce serait bien.
examples.translation: If you came when I invite you, it would be nice.

examples.sentence: Le colis est envoyé quand le paiement est reçu.
examples.translation: The package is sent when the payment is received.

entries.intro: Interrogative adverb of reason or subordinating conjunction.
entries.usage: Invariable. Written as a single word. 'le pourquoi' (the reason why).

examples.translation: Why are you laughing?

examples.sentence: Il demande pourquoi tu es parti.
examples.translation: He asks why you left.

examples.sentence: Si je comprenais pourquoi il agit ainsi, je l'aiderais.
examples.translation: If I understood why he acts this way, I would help him.

examples.sentence: On ignore pourquoi la route a été fermée.
examples.translation: It is unknown why the road was closed.

entries.intro: Interrogative adverb of manner or state. Often used to ask about health or ask for clarification.
entries.usage: Invariable. Triggers 't' liaison.

examples.translation: How are you?
How to make this cake?

examples.sentence: Si je savais comment résoudre ce problème, je le ferais.
examples.translation: If I knew how to solve this problem, I would do it.

examples.sentence: On montre comment le moteur est construit.
examples.translation: They show how the engine is built.

entries.intro: Refers to a different person or object. Can function as adjective or indefinite pronoun.
entries.usage: agrees in number: autre (sing), autres (plur). 'un autre' (another), 'l'autre' (the other).

examples.translation: I want another book.
The others have already left.
Another solution would be preferable.
The other option is chosen.

entries.intro: Adjective indicating identity (same) or adverb indicating emphasis (even). Placed after pronouns to mean '-self' (moi-même).
entries.usage: As adjective, takes plural 's' (mêmes). As adverb, invariable.

examples.translation: We have the same car. (Adjective)
Even the children know it.

examples.sentence: Si c'était le même prix, je l'achèterais.
examples.translation: If it were the same price, I would buy it.

examples.sentence: La même règle est appliquée partout.
examples.translation: The same rule is applied everywhere.

entries.intro: Adjective meaning 'some' (singular) or 'a few' (plural). Can also function as adverb meaning 'about/approximately'.
entries.usage: Plural form is 'quelques' (extremely common, meaning 'a few / some').

examples.translation: I have a few friends in Paris.
There is some misunderstanding.

examples.sentence: Si j'avais quelques jours de congé, je partirais.
examples.translation: If I had a few days off, I would leave.
A few errors are corrected.

entries.intro: Indefinite pronoun indicating the absence of everything. Used with negative particle 'ne' (#5) in negation.
entries.usage: Pronoun. 'rien ne...' (nothing as subject). 'de rien' (you're welcome).

examples.translation: I know nothing.
Nothing is easy.

examples.sentence: Si je n'avais rien à faire, je dormirais.
examples.translation: If I had nothing to do, I would sleep.
Nothing is lost.

entries.intro: Adverb of time indicating negation (never, paired with 'ne') or condition (ever).
entries.usage: Paired with 'ne' for negation. Standing alone, it can mean 'ever' in conditional/question clauses.

examples.sentence: Je ne bois jamais de café.
examples.translation: I never drink coffee.

examples.sentence: Si jamais tu le vois, dis-le moi.
examples.translation: If ever you see him, tell me. (Condition)

examples.sentence: Si je ne voyageais jamais, je serais triste.
examples.translation: If I never traveled, I would be sad.
The lesson is never forgotten.

entries.intro: Adverb of frequency meaning 'always', or indicating continuity (still).
entries.usage: Invariable adverb. Opposes 'jamais' (#89).

examples.translation: He is always late.
I am still waiting for his answer.

examples.sentence: Si tu m'aimais toujours, tu resterais.
examples.translation: If you still loved me, you would stay.
The rules are always respected.

entries.intro: Adverb of frequency indicating that an event occurs frequently.
entries.usage: Invariable. Often placed after the conjugated verb.

examples.translation: I often go to the cinema.
It rains often in London.

examples.sentence: Si nous nous voyions plus souvent, nous serions plus proches.
examples.translation: If we saw each other more often, we would be closer.
The question is often asked.

entries.intro: Refers to physical/mental effort or a professional occupation. Cross-referenced with 'maison' (#93) and 'nom' (#94).
entries.usage: le travail, les travaux (highly irregular plural form 'travaux').

examples.translation: I like my work.

examples.sentence: Les travaux sur la route ont commencé.
examples.translation: The roadworks have started.

examples.sentence: Un travail plus intéressant me plairait.
examples.translation: A more interesting job would please me.

examples.sentence: Le travail est terminé à temps.
examples.translation: The work is completed on time.

entries.intro: A building for human habitation, or the concept of household/firm. Cross-referenced with 'travail' (#92).
entries.usage: la maison, les maisons. 'fait maison' (homemade).

examples.translation: It is a beautiful house.

examples.sentence: Je reste à la maison ce soir.
examples.translation: I am staying at home tonight.

examples.sentence: Une maison plus grande conviendrait à la famille.
examples.translation: A bigger house would suit the family.

examples.sentence: La maison est repeinte en blanc.
examples.translation: The house is repainted in white.

entries.intro: A word by which a person, animal, place, or thing is designated (name), or a word class in grammar (noun).
entries.usage: le nom, les noms. 'nom de famille' (last name), 'prénom' (first name).

examples.translation: What is your name?
It is a proper noun.

examples.sentence: Si je connaissais son nom, je l'appellerais.
examples.translation: If I knew his/her name, I would call him/her.

examples.sentence: Le nom est inscrit sur la liste.
examples.translation: The name is written on the list.

entries.intro: A female parent. Cross-referenced with masculine 'père' (#96) and 'fils' (#97) / 'fille' (#98).
entries.usage: la mère, les mères. 'grand-mère' (grandmother).

examples.translation: My mother cooks very well.
She is a good mother.

examples.sentence: Si ma mère était là, elle saurait quoi faire.
examples.translation: If my mother were here, she would know what to do.

examples.sentence: La mère est fêtée en mai.
examples.translation: Mother is celebrated in May.

entries.intro: A male parent. Cross-referenced with feminine 'mère' (#95).
entries.usage: le père, les pères. 'grand-père' (grandfather).

examples.translation: My father works as an engineer.
He is a devoted father.

examples.sentence: Si mon père le permettait, je sortirais.
examples.translation: If my father permitted it, I would go out.

examples.sentence: Le père est respecté par ses enfants.
examples.translation: The father is respected by his children.

entries.intro: A male child in relation to his parents. Cross-referenced with feminine 'fille' (#98).
entries.usage: le fils, les fils (pronounciation: final 's' is always pronounced, 'fiss').

examples.sentence: Il est le fils unique de la famille.
examples.translation: He is the only son of the family.
His/Her son is ten years old.

examples.sentence: Un fils plus obéissant aiderait ses parents.
examples.translation: A more obedient son would help his parents.

examples.sentence: Le fils est éduqué avec rigueur.
examples.translation: The son is educated with rigor.

entries.intro: A female child or young woman. Cross-referenced with masculine 'fils' (#97) and 'garçon' (boy).
entries.usage: la fille, les filles. 'jeune fille' (young girl).

examples.translation: She is his/her eldest daughter.

examples.sentence: Il y a une fille dans la cour.
examples.translation: There is a girl in the yard.

examples.sentence: Une fille plus âgée pourrait garder les enfants.
examples.translation: An older girl could babysit the children.
The young girl is rewarded.

entries.intro: A nation state, territory, or region.
entries.usage: le pays, les pays (plural spelling and pronunciation remain the same).

examples.sentence: La France est un beau pays.
examples.translation: France is a beautiful country.
He travels to several countries.

examples.sentence: Un pays plus solidaire surmonterait la crise.
examples.translation: A more united country would overcome the crisis.
The country is governed democratically.

entries.intro: Refers to the current day or modern times.
entries.usage: Invariable. Compound spelling with apostrophe.

examples.translation: Today the weather is beautiful.

examples.sentence: Je commence mon nouveau travail aujourd'hui.
examples.translation: I start my new job today.

examples.sentence: Aujourd'hui serait un bon jour pour commencer.
examples.translation: Today would be a good day to start.
The report will be presented today.
